headline: Nvidia RTX 5080 prices hit $2,000, costing more than RTX 5090 launch
summary: The Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 is now selling for up to $2,000, surpassing the RTX 5090's original MSRP and with limited stock available.
details: The Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080, previously the second-fastest GPU in Nvidia's lineup, is now fetching prices as high as $2,000, matching the launch MSRP of the RTX 5090. This significant price increase means consumers are paying two to three times the GPU's original launch price.

Finding an RTX 5080 in stock is challenging, with most available units coming from third-party sellers at inflated prices. For example, a PNY RTX 5080 is listed at $1,999 on Best Buy, while other models from Asus and Gigabyte are priced at $2,299.99 and $2,983.23 respectively.

The scarcity extends to physical retail locations, with limited stock often available for in-store pickup only. Prices at retailers like Micro Center reflect this, with some models listed around $1,979.99. Many online listings are from less reputable third-party sellers, further complicating the purchase process.

The surge in RTX 5080 prices is indicative of a broader trend affecting the entire RTX 50-series, with prices steadily climbing since launch. This marks the first time the RTX 5080's price floor has reached the RTX 5090's initial MSRP, a stark contrast to its average price of around $1,500 just a few months ago.

This price escalation is attributed to increased demand for high-end GPUs, partly driven by the AI market. Nvidia's focus has shifted towards enterprise AI solutions, impacting memory manufacturers' allocations. This diversion of resources towards high-margin AI hardware has reduced the availability of memory chips for consumer graphics cards.
